When passing on the road, I was able to see wooden crosses, and there would be as many crosses as people buried. Naturally these were not proper crosses. These were improvised ones, created on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When it comes to the burial of these victims, did you have any body-bags, did you have any coffins, or anything else to put the bodies in?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA MEDAKOVIC
utterances.text: I already spoke about this problem. As I told you, we had no funeral equipment whatsoever, not even for our people. Our soldiers were buried without that. We had no funeral equipment and no carpenters who could make coffins. We had no body-bags. There was nobody to supply them for us. That is to say, that these people were buried as they were found. They were simply placed in the ground. Naturally I believed this to be a temporary measure and I expected, because we were constantly in contact with the negotiating team that negotiated with the Croatian side. The Croatian side, however, never sought these corpses that were buried around Saborsko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the main church in Saborsko was damaged? You mentioned this large church in the centre of the village; this is how you described it.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA MEDAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was damaged. When passing on the road, I could see that it was damaged. However, I also know that the person who had brought in the reinforcement, the infamous Luka Hodak, deployed forces there, and turned this church into observation point and machine-gun mess, since it was quite firmly built, they stored ammunition there, the artillery ammunition. It is a bit odd for Croatia, which is a mostly Catholic country, that such a man, who is not a Catholic, was appointed commander. He's a member of some sect, and I have nothing against sects, but he is a member of Hare Krishna sect, and they found a man like that in Zagreb and appointed him the commander in Saborsko. The real residents of Saborsko were proper Croats, Catholics. They had respect for their church, and I don't believe that any of the residents of Saborsko would turn their own church into an ammunition depot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In relation what was confiscated in Plaski, do you know what happened to agricultural equipment, to tractors and trailers?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA MEDAKOVIC
utterances.text: I think you made a mistake. You said Plaski.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, I meant Saborsko.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA MEDAKOVIC
utterances.text: Commander Trbovic issued an order for the military police, together with civilian police, to confiscate any equipment stolen by these people, and to bring it to the factory compound in the town. A commission was established which was supposed to do this and to monitor this. We had problems with criminals. However, I think that this task was done well. There was some property that was stolen. However, I know that the order of Colonel Trbovic was strictly complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, does this mean what you just told us, does this mean that these items which had been stolen from Saborsko, were taken away, were confiscated from the people who had stolen them, and that this was done pursuant to the order of Colonel Trbovic?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA MEDAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. That's what they did. Naturally they couldn't restore every single item that was stolen but the majority of it. I have to say that since the majority of the population left that area, left Saborsko, and the road leading to Slunj was open, was passable, a lot of the equipment left with the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, in relation to the church that you mentioned, was there a Catholic church in Plaski?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA MEDAKOVIC
utterances.text: In the very centre of Plaski there was a Catholic church of Saint Ann. It was not damaged at all. Maybe something was stolen from the church, but I don't think so, because there wasn't much to steal. And all of the residents in that street -- and there were Croats residing there and all of those Croats who lived there in 1991 were still there in 1995. They lived and worked with us. Some of them even worked together with me at the municipality. That church was left intact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Before you go on, the agricultural equipment and tractors and trailers that you referred to that were stolen by these people, which people were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mentioned that after the end of the operation, everybody who was involved in the operation withdrew, including the tanks, tanks went to the training grounds. My unit went back to its tasks and as did other people. However, those people who were not involved in the operations, who were thieves - and I never concealed the fact that we had such people among us - those were people without conscience. And when we had power outages and everything was covered by darkness, this was a fertile ground for them to operate in, and I regret not having any mechanisms to prevent them from doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: So were they part of your unit? Or did they belong to any unit? Or were they civilians? I'm not understanding completely. What and who were they? Granted that they were acting against your wishes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's hard for me to speculate, but based on the people from whom such equipment was confiscated, I know that they came from everywhere, from Licka Jesenica, and from other places, and even from Vojinovac, which is some 20 or 30 kilometres away. So this wasn't a limited group that went around stealing, no. It was the people who stole in peacetime, and they continued doing that in wartime. Perhaps the circumstances contributed to the increase in their numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you also said: I never concealed the fact that we had such people among us. Did you have them among you? I think this is the question that the Judge is trying to establish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much, Judge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I say "among us," I'm referring to the entire population. In Plaski at the time there was six to 7.000 residents, and there were between 1.000 and 1.200 soldiers. So there were women, there were minors, there were the elderly that were not part of this. I can't tell you that there were only saints in the Plaski brigade. You have to put things into perspective. You have to understand the circumstances when this happened, and looking back, it seems that this was planned in advance, but I'm telling you that these were sporadic incidents, and it is my personal desire to find all such culprits and punish them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you for the time being. Yes, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps I'm going to have one more question or two, but I'm very near the end of my examination-in-chief. Since it's the end of business for today, I'm not going to proceed tonight. I think I should leave it for tomorrow, since my learned friend will have cross-examination to do too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. Can we hold you down to a maximum of two questions tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This brings us to the end of the day. We will adjourn until tomorrow. Now to this month's -- we start at 9.00 tomorrow, in Courtroom I. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on the 10th day of October, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
